That is a real
  suspicion and not a verified defect, and changing a write path on a suspicion would trade a known
  quantity for an unknown one. Recording it in the allowlist keeps it visible to whoever next opens
  that file instead of relying on someone rediscovering it.

an allowlist entry that says only "legacy" would reproduce the problem the file
  exists to prevent, which is why the test asserts each reason is substantive.

The allowlist counts are asserted exactly, so a new bypass in an already-listed module fails
  just as loudly as one in a new module.

Trace is a distinct product line on top of the `memory-seed` engine; a distinct top-level name
  is the whole point of moving off "Trail" onto its own brand.

the command drops the `memory-seed-` prefix so it
  won't appear under `memory-seed`+Tab discovery - the intended cost of a standalone brand, mitigated
  by core-package docs cross-linking.

Set `memory-trace` as the canonical package and command name for the Memory Trace companion
  distribution everywhere it was previously written as `memory-seed-trace` (target/tentative):
  the Trace product plan (Part 1 decision, acceptance criterion, resolved open question),
  the distribution plan (Phase 2 target + retrieval-API surface + Phase 2 acceptance criterion),
  `3.0-plan.md` (package split list, B1 API section + command example, sequencing item 3),
  `NEXT_STEPS.md`, and `docs/functionality-audit.md`.

Kept `memory-seed-trace` referenced in the Trace plan only as (a) the historical availability
  table, (b) explicit "not this name" statements, and (c) an optional defensive alias if a redirect
  is ever wanted.

The legend prints these labels verbatim, and `str.title()` rendered `mcp-tools` as "Mcp Tools"

  shipping the same labels through the API unread.

Rather than transcribe the bodies, the successors were confirmed independently: all seven were retired
  in one commit (`0fc64cba`), whose entry `mse_ddba1ztxqhasfbwf` names the destinations in its own D2/D3
  — "fold Evidence Envelope, Capability Status, and seeded docs lifecycle into their existing owners" and
  "combine worktree GC and naming/lifecycle policy... and its two superseded source proposals". That
  raises the evidence above each document's self-claim.

`memory-seed-semantic-workflow-exploration-index.md` points at the **entry id**,
  not a path: it split four ways, so no single successor exists, and the schema reserves entry ids for
  exactly the case where a decision retired a document rather than a document replacing it.

500/1k/10k datasets are generated on demand - the
  generator IS the committed fixture; megabytes of synthetic markdown would be review noise.

Roadmap Phase 0 requires "500, 1,000 and 10,000-entry synthetic datasets" before any
  migration work; determinism makes future parity measurements reproducible.

Same (count, seed) ->
  byte-identical .memory-seed/sessions tree (month-grouped, real schema); shape exercises the
  Trail's full grammar - main line, up to 3 parallel feature branches with bounded lifetimes
  (forks/merges/daisy-chains emerge), related/supersedes/evolves edges (forward-only),
  topics, varied prose for search ranking.

Rows are now
  overview-first: search cards show date + title only (score appears only under a query; excerpt,
  topics, agent, matched-section chips moved to the reader), timeline items collapsed to one
  time+title line

The dense-UI research brief's top levers (overview-first, data-ink, Hick's law, facet
  hygiene, muted-by-default) applied per the user's "too crowded - simplify" direction and
  explicit approval of the recommended options.

the redundant timestamp prefix is stripped from all list titles via
  `stripTitleStamp()` (the date/time column already carries it).
This proves package delivery and comparable interaction without prematurely routing the shipped Graph tab through a candidate renderer.
Serve a bundled vis-network/Cytoscape.js comparison at `/benchmarks/renderer`, with both adapters consuming the bounded renderer-neutral fixture and no external resource requests.

`sessions/links/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` sidecars are part of the effective graph contract, so MCP tools should not remain YAML-only while Trace and `links check` see union(YAML, sidecar). The shared merge point belongs in `memory_seed.retrieval`, which already depends on `semantic_cache`; putting it there avoids a reverse import from `semantic_cache` into retrieval.
